a new feature  similar like [qcut](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.qcut.html)
comments: @marcvanheerden would you like this one? It are completely new algorithms.

Cool! They can be added to the `polars-ops` crate and trait.

Then via tvat it can be exposed in lazy. Thanks for your help. :)
Apologies for the delay, will get going with a draft PR this week
Apologies for the long break here, looks like cut was implemented in #4715. @ritchie46 can I add qcut?
I guess `cut` and `qcut` would be very convenient functions, ideally applicable as expressions on lazy dataframes.

> I guess `cut` and `qcut` would be very convenient functions, ideally applicable as expressions on lazy dataframes.

I think so

Clearly interested in this. I think `qcut` is very important. The usual use-case in Finance is to do a `qcut()` within a given group. Say, every month, compute the decile group of a given variable. I am not sure who to do this in `polars` right now whereas I do this very efficiently in Pandas. 

A very useful binning function related to `qcut()` is `ntile` in R (https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/ntile.html). I hope both can be implemented soon in `polars`.

Thanks!

@alexander-beedie @ritchie46 this is great! 

one suggestion though: for a moment I thought I could use `qcut` in the same exact way I most people use it with pandas, that is the with argument `labels = False`. This is an important one because then labels are comparables across groups (say decile 10 is always decile 10 no matter the group, while in reality they could correspond to different numeric intervals, say [2, inf] and [8, 12] depending on the values in each group). 

Right now the only way to achieve that is to manually create a list of string labels... and feed them to `labels`. This is a bit cumbersome when we iterate over the number of quantiles for instance. Do you think you would implement the default labels (int numbers from 0 to the number of quantiles minus 1) automatically? This little change would be immensely useful.

Thanks
